spine.active_goal: Get Field Notes through its first Google Play review with a closed testing (Alpha) release, so the temporary name 'dev.satanshumishra.field_notes (unreviewed)' becomes "Field Notes" and the app stops being a Draft app. Per decision 01M4RZJMBA5A6245755SZ8KGWK (option B, owner 2026-10-12), the release sent for review is 1.0.1, whose Play bundle leaves sync out, so it needs no foreground service declaration. Sending for review happens only on the owner's yes.
spine.next_step: Work on option B (decision 01M4RZJMBA5A6245755SZ8KGWK) when the owner says start. Run it through the pipeline from the user's checkout on main (at 7a8fbce7 since the owner pulled on 2026-10-12; its uncommitted changes are in docs/prototype/ and tool/probe/macos/drive.sh, none in files B touches) with the interphase feature pathway, using the decision's outcome as the scope. Move the upload Kotlin and its manifest entries behind the fieldNotesSelfUpdate switch, add a store stand-in UploadChannel, hide Sync & storage on Play copies, add a dated 1.0.1 CHANGELOG section, and prove it with a test plus a merged-manifest check of the built AAB. After the PR merges, tag v1.0.1 only on the owner's yes. Then in Play Console, confirm the 1.0.1 draft replaced the 1.0.0 one on Alpha and re-enter the release notes. Check that no foreground service declaration is still asked for, and that Data safety and App access match. Next and Save, then Send for review only on the owner's yes. After approval, confirm c1 and delete PLAY_RELEASE_STATUS for c2. The data-sync video (build/play/field-notes-data-sync-upload.mp4) is now unused and kept only as a fallback for option A.
spine.last_session: 2026-10-12: Release run 38295781439 succeeded and published the v1.0.0 GitHub release (macOS DMG, Windows, Android APK with the self-updater), and the Play job uploaded the 1.0.0 AAB as a draft to Closed testing, Alpha. In Play Console the draft's en-US release notes are saved, but Next and Save stop on the missing FOREGROUND_SERVICE_DATA_SYNC declaration. Nothing was sent for review, on the owner's instruction. The demo video for that declaration (build/play/field-notes-data-sync-upload.mp4) was recorded in the lab and approved by the owner, but never uploaded. Research on Play's 12 testers for 14 days rule for personal accounts created after 2023-11-13 is done: open testing is locked until production access, organization accounts are exempt, and F-Droid or IzzyOnDroid are alternatives. The owner chose option B (decision 01M4RZJMBA5A6245755SZ8KGWK). The owner's S24 Ultra and Mac were reinstalled fresh from the v1.0.0 GitHub release, so they keep sync and self-update. Option B has not been started.

open_risks.text: Unverified: Play may still ask for the FOREGROUND_SERVICE_DATA_SYNC declaration after 1.0.1 if any other bundle still on a track requests it. The 1.0.0 AAB stays in the Alpha draft until 1.0.1 replaces it, and Internal testing holds an inactive draft, release 7 (1.0.0-rc.2), that probably requests it. Check App content and each track after the 1.0.1 upload. Discarding the rc.2 draft is the owner's call.

Unverified: a 1.0.1 upload with release status draft is expected to replace the 1.0.0 draft on Alpha. If it does, the saved en-US release notes need re-entering for 1.0.1. If it adds a second draft instead, the 1.0.0 draft needs discarding (owner's call).

WorkManager 2.11.0 is used only by the upload code (android/app/build.gradle.kts:70 implementation androidx.work:work-runtime). Its library manifest merges an untyped FOREGROUND_SERVICE permission and SystemForegroundService into any build that depends on it. The Play build must either drop the dependency (selfUpdate-only) or remove those entries with tools:node=remove, and the proof must read the merged manifest of the built AAB, not the source manifests.

Play Console's Data safety and App access answers may describe sync. After 1.0.1, check that they match a Play build with no sync; App access 'All functionality available without special access' becomes true.
